title: HumanEval Pro and MBPP Pro: Evaluating Large Language Models on Self-invoking Code Generation Task

model.params_source: paper Sec. 4 (temperature 0.2 for all API models; greedy only for open-source models); max_tokens/top_p assumed; API name Table 10

task.approximation: pass@1 from one sample per item per seed at temperature 0.2, as in the paper.

items.config_or_split: default / train (164 rows verified; fields id, raw_problem, new_problem, raw_solution, new_solution, test_code)

fields_paper.label: test_code (assert statements run against the generated file)

output.postprocess: execute test_code in a sandbox; pass if every assert passes
output.parse_paper: python code block(s) extracted from the response (CodeEval-Pro sanitizer); the file must define both functions

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: pass@1 = share of the 164 problems whose generated file passes all test_code asserts (one sample)
metric.judge: rule: execution of test_code with the CodeEval-Pro evalpro harness
metric.original_location: Table 2, row GPT-4-Turbo, column HumanEval Pro (0-shot)

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare --dry-run 2026-09-07 (chars/4 input tokens, max_tokens counted as output per call)

open_points: no hook: pass@1 requires executing the model-generated Python file against test_code (CodeEval-Pro evalpro harness) - an execution sandbox for untrusted code; prompt and generation are otherwise machine-ready (--prepare renders the 164 prompts).
